original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract, not another mixture already covered by the frozen catalogue.

first_step.inspect: Read the frozen catalogue bound exclusions and select one genuinely different helper endpoint inventory.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write the complete optimistic child histogram and reject it immediately if even the relaxation has insufficient headroom.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Helper inventory changes can improve the moment; repacking a covered cost interface cannot evade its scoped bound.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.

actual_scope: Price the optimistic child histogram for replacing all 122 selected gauge44 width-8 helpers by width-6 helpers, preserving excess 1856 by deleting 244 rank-1 children per call and concentrating the freed width into rank-48 residuals. Reject the edit if that relaxation does not clear 1/99.
scope_change_reason: The card allows one helper type with explicit counts. Width 6 is outside the frozen catalogue alphabet and the selected inventory. The physical contract is not claimed; the first experiment is the optimistic histogram, and it misses the 1/99 planning budget.
bottleneck_link: The complex primitive binds. A narrower helper inventory can raise that primitive only by moving rank mass into cheaper children. This relaxation is the favorable version of one such move, and it remains far below the budget needed for kappa above 0.01.
stop_rule: Stop when the optimistic root is certified below 1/99. Do not build a width-6 circuit for the kappa greater than 0.01 target.
evidence: PASS_SELECTED_WIDTH6_NARROWING. Width-6 root 1760855940405956673857/10^24 is strictly above the selected root 1675462676808103522925/10^24 and strictly below 1/99. Same-mass width changes do not beat the concentrated-idle root 1682094870064815352349/10^24.
author: Riquelme Soares
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance was used to choose the edit, derive the optimistic histogram, and write the verifier. The arithmetic was checked by the pinned moment engine.

open_questions.question: Can the scalar word narrow those 122 width-8 helpers to width 6 while deleting exactly 244 rank-1 children and no other paid rank?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That realization is the gap between this upper bound and a complex-root increase of about five percent. The bound already shows the increase cannot reach 1/99.
open_questions.first_step: Locate one width-8 helper's gates in the k8 slots word and test whether two rank-1 children are local to it.
open_questions.blocked_by: The admitted width alphabet has no width-6 operation, and this package does not construct one.

open_questions.question: Does the selected T16 owner geometry contain a bin larger than 48?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A larger residual would make concentration more favorable and could retire this upper bound.
open_questions.first_step: Read the pattern capacities from the T16 owner certificate and record the maximum bin rank.
open_questions.blocked_by: This check matches only the catalogue capacity total to the selected idle-plus-helper mass. It does not parse OWNERS.json.gz.
